## Overview

Run supported target-conditioned own-KV EAGLE3/MTP speculators in a standalone GPU process using native MRV2 execution. Include native checkpoint loading, contract and model-level regression coverage with the runtime.

Based on [vllm-project/vllm#63333](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63333). Related design: [RFC #42109](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42109). This is part 2/3 (GPU execution) of the standalone placement series.

## Claims

- Load native draft weights and compatible shared target embedding/head tensors, including Nemotron checkpoint aliases, then warm prefill and decode before admission.
- Maintain draft KV across chunked prefill, rejection, row reordering and effective K=0..capacity; reject insufficient effective draft context before native execution.
- Verify remote proposals through the native target path and test supported MTP loading, feature contracts and standalone/native model behavior in the same increment.
- Exercise real socket-cleanup failure through the public LLM API, checking exact target-only continuation, terminal request fencing and remote recovery for a fresh request.

## Validation

Source: `70b612c1a8fb489c841992ee4ad1126af4b4b9d3`. Review base: `0085c631c160cb47142457f5f812980e92ba1552`. [Incremental diff](https://github.com/seo-rii/vllm/compare/0085c631c160cb47142457f5f812980e92ba1552...70b612c1a8fb489c841992ee4ad1126af4b4b9d3).

This corrective revision retains the existing PR boundaries. New results below cover only their named source and test selection; inherited coverage is labeled explicitly. Overlapping runs are not added together.

Complete foundation and GPU-runtime CPU suite: **874 passed, 5 skipped**, executed at `ddd9f08b0d8d388d0d6cc478bd762a3f88712c6e`. This is inherited coverage from the stated tested source; this result is not a separate execution of this PR head.

CPU execution used PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu and the allowed Transformers 5.20.2 / huggingface_hub 1.33.0 dependency pair. Tracked source hashes were identical before and after execution.

Skips are existing CUDA-only cases; this corrective revision adds no skip or rerun markers.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -B -m pytest --noconftest -q tests/v1/spec_decode/remote/
```

Standalone MTP public-LLM socket cleanup and recovery: **1 passed, 0 skipped**, executed at `70b612c1a8fb489c841992ee4ad1126af4b4b9d3`. This run executed this exact PR head.

Executed on one A100 80GB with PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130. Tracked source and native-artifact hashes matched before and after execution; all owned workers retired.

The affected request finishes with exactly the target-only output and remains terminal with no extra remote RPCs or consumed drafts; a fresh request reconnects and consumes additional remote drafts.

Original production `1dbbf419a716325eb71eb38aff236eec60f24dbd` plus the regression tests (validation-only snapshot `535a0fc22fff812958bbfad332b6428a9d1685be`) reported `1 failed, 0 passed, 0 skipped` for the reported defect. RED command: `.venv/bin/python -B -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -v -r s -s -p pytest_asyncio.plugin -p pytest_forked tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/remote/test_remote_mtp.py::test_remote_mtp_socket_cleanup_failure_preserves_target_only_and_reconnects`.

RED output: `RuntimeError: remote drafter proposal failed: OSError: [Errno 9] Bad file descriptor`. The GREEN regression completes without this failure.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -B -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -v -r s -s -p pytest_asyncio.plugin -p pytest_forked tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/remote/test_remote_mtp.py::test_remote_mtp_socket_cleanup_failure_preserves_target_only_and_reconnects
```

<details>
<summary>Previous-source validation before this corrective revision</summary>

The following results retain their original SHAs and hardware scope. They are historical evidence, not fresh executions of the source above.

Previously published source: `1dbbf419a716325eb71eb38aff236eec60f24dbd`. Review base: `e888ffdb493c9b75e12df4612cf6d68e830d8086`. [Incremental diff](https://github.com/seo-rii/vllm/compare/e888ffdb493c9b75e12df4612cf6d68e830d8086...1dbbf419a716325eb71eb38aff236eec60f24dbd).

CPU complete remote suite: **712 passed, 3 skipped**, executed at `bc1d2210d7e078537bc089007a5fc8150e89cde5`. 

Real model and public LLM regressions: **25 passed, 0 skipped** at the previously published source `1dbbf419a716325eb71eb38aff236eec60f24dbd` on one A100 80GB. Owned test/server processes were retired after execution.

The model checks use target-only and native local MTP controls, real checkpoints/loaders, chunked prefill, rejection/reuse, and separate-checkpoint settings. The short-draft public constructor must fail at the context contract before remote native execution. Dense-attention target controls require exact token IDs; hybrid/MLA target controls use the existing top-5 logprob comparison, while native/remote placement requires exact token IDs. Callable model observations explicitly use the existing trusted-test serialization fixture. Seeded checkpoints validate placement/state; the trained MiMo case separately requires positive acceptance.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -B -m pytest \
  -p pytest_asyncio.plugin -p pytest_forked -v -s \
  tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/remote/test_remote_mtp.py \
  -k 'test_remote_mtp or test_remote_native_mtp or test_hyv3_mtp or test_separate_mtp_checkpoint'
```

<details>
<summary>Historical validation at the stated source revisions</summary>

These executions predate the assembled source above and do not substitute for current-source validation.

### Evidence from `9335084f3bf73f55f3e822658f92fdea6f37c241` and earlier stated sources

Previously validated source `9335084f3b`, validated on one A100 80GB:

- Remote CPU/socket and CUDA suite: **668 passed, 0 skipped**. All three CUDA shared-weight storage cases ran. The public-config draft-context rejection regression also passed.
- Real MiMo-7B-RL MTP K1: **1 passed**, using inline. Target-only and remote token IDs matched for prompt lengths 15/16/17/65 in both request orders (8 remote requests per transport, 16 generated tokens each). Drafted and accepted token counters were positive. The test covers chunked prefill and completed-request reuse, with greedy BF16/eager execution, FlashAttention, target TP1 + draft TP1 in separate processes on the same GPU, a 5000 ms request timeout and `failure_policy="error"`.

Environment: Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, Transformers 5.19.0 and huggingface_hub 2.2.0; model-test cleanup also used orjson 3.13.0 from the repository's declared requirements. The MiMo checkpoint revision remains `6299b5a2c45daf0c429285c92b8e61a5bd011c0d`.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -B -m pytest --noconftest -v -r s \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/remote/

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -B -m pytest \
  -v -s -p pytest_asyncio -p pytest_forked \
  tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/remote/
```

Earlier CPU/socket, native-local and model comparison results below retain their original source SHAs. The Qwen3 EAGLE3 results were not rerun in this validation.

CPU/socket suite at `f59dcb96c3`: **657 passed, 3 CUDA skips**.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" \
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest -q \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/remote/
```

GPU integration at `f59dcb96c3` used one A100 80GB with separate target/draft processes, TP1+TP1, greedy BF16/eager, batch invariance, a 5000 ms timeout and `failure_policy="error"`. Target-only, native local and remote inline each ran 14 requests with 16 output tokens per model. The target session confirmed valid remote proposals.

| Model | K | Native and remote vs target-only | Drafted / accepted, native = inline |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MiMo-7B-RL MTP | 1 | 224/224 token IDs match | 144 / 70 |
| Qwen3-8B EAGLE3 | 3 | 224/224 token IDs match | 395 / 88 |

The checked-in MiMo smoke test exercises real model execution, chunked prefill, positive acceptance and request reuse:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
  tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/remote/
```

### Evidence from `fe0efa4262dd2dce7cb443af2169be599cc8bb2d` and earlier stated sources

Historical validation source: `2ecb42be878dc2ee1eb89678896c37a7d316128f`, based on #12 at `1914b5f7e64955da4ba0a894af11f114c24b166e`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Nemotron alias regression | Before: 8 failed, 6 passed; after: 14 passed |
| Two consecutive CPU checkpoint-loading tests | Before: 1 failed, 1 passed; after: 2 passed |
| Final-head CPU suite | 1,415 passed, 15 CUDA-dependent cases skipped (`--noconftest`) |
| Seeded model execution on one A100 80GB | 15 passed; 135 requests and 1,080 output tokens per mode, native/remote exactly equal |
| Trained MiMo remote execution on the same GPU | 2 repository tests passed: inline and CUDA IPC |
| Trained MiMo native control | One separate external control passed; 8 requests / 128 output tokens equal to target-only |

The 15 seeded cases cover Exaone full/sliding attention, GLM4-MoE, Qwen3Next, Nemotron-H, HYV3 and dense-MLA GLM4-MoE-Lite at K=1/3, plus ERNIE K=1. Native and remote counters match per case (totals: **937 proposals / 1,815 draft tokens / 8 accepted tokens**). Both MLA cases also have identical returned top-5 logprobs. GLM4-MoE-Lite K=1 differs from target-only at two token positions in both native and remote; the unchanged native top-5 candidate comparison passes. All other cases have zero target-only token differences.

Trained control: `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-7B-RL@6299b5a2c45daf0c429285c92b8e61a5bd011c0d`, BF16, K=1, target/draft TP1, eager MRV2, FLASH_ATTN, prompt lengths 15/16/17/65, original and reversed request order. Native, remote inline and same-GPU IPC each match target-only on **128 output tokens**, with **66 proposals / 66 draft tokens / 58 accepted tokens**. Remote tests use strict failure policy and a 5-second request timeout. All owned draft processes exited; locks were released and no GPU compute process remained after either campaign.

Reproduction:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest -q tests/v1/spec_decode/remote/
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/spec_decode/remote/test_mtp_contracts.py \
  -k 'nemotron_shared_embedding or tied_nemotron or conflicting_nemotron'
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -s \
  tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/remote/test_remote_mtp.py::test_remote_native_mtp_matches_native_and_target
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -s \
  'tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/remote/test_remote_mtp.py::test_remote_mtp_matches_target_and_uses_drafts[inline-False-1]' \
  'tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/remote/test_remote_mtp.py::test_remote_mtp_matches_target_and_uses_drafts[cuda_ipc-False-1]'
```

The small seeded checkpoints test loading, execution and state handling. They are untrained and do not establish checkpoint quality or useful acceptance. Trained MiMo evidence is reported separately. The hardware scope is one physical GPU; this PR makes no throughput, cross-GPU IPC or TP2 claim.

</details>

</details>

## Details

Standalone MTP requires the draft's effective `ModelConfig.max_model_len` to cover the target limit. Contract validation rejects a shorter draft before native model execution. Model-level tests accompany the runtime and exercise native constructors/loaders, shared-weight identity and real target/native/remote comparisons.

Execution is same-host, greedy and eager, with draft TP1. Prefix caching, async scheduling, streaming input, LoRA and multimodal requests remain restricted for this backend. The native model implementations perform computation; this change supplies process placement and its state contract.

The intended benefit is target GPU memory relief and placement flexibility, following the [MTP offload question in the RFC](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42109#issuecomment-4561513801). Compare performance with native local MTP/EAGLE3 as well as target-only execution. Separate processes can add transfer and preparation latency, and a dedicated draft device increases total memory use. More available target KV does not by itself establish a larger supported context length. This increment does not implement the RFC's predictive fan-out cache or claim target/draft compute overlap.

AI assistance: Codex and Claude Code were used for implementation and testing. Human review of the final diff remains pending.

---

<summary>Pull Request Checklist</summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill.
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [ ] **Design Fit:** Maintainer agreement on the runtime boundary and supported contracts.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Review current-source validation, model evidence and remaining hardware gaps.
- [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Human review of the final code and documentation.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Scope, claims, validation and tradeoffs are documented.
</details>

Remote tests use strict failure policy and a 5-second request timeout. All owned draft processes exited; locks were released and no GPU compute process remained after either campaign.

Reproduction:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest -q tests/v1/spec_decode/remote/
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/spec_decode/remote/test_mtp_contracts.py \
  -k 'nemotron_shared_embedding or tied_nemotron or conflicting_nemotron'
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -s \
  tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/remote/test_remote_mtp.py::test_remote_native_mtp_matches_native_and_target
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -s \
  'tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/remote/test_remote_mtp.py::test_remote_mtp_matches_target_and_uses_drafts[inline-False-1]' \
  'tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/remote/test_remote_mtp.py::test_remote_mtp_matches_target_and_uses_drafts[cuda_ipc-False-1]'
```

The small seeded checkpoints test loading, execution and state handling. They are untrained and do not establish checkpoint quality or useful acceptance. Trained MiMo evidence is reported separately. The hardware scope is one physical GPU; this PR makes no throughput, cross-GPU IPC or TP2 claim.

</details>

</details>

## Details

Standalone MTP requires the draft's effective `ModelConfig.max_model_len` to cover the target limit. Contract validation rejects a shorter draft before native model execution. Model-level tests accompany the runtime and exercise native constructors/loaders, shared-weight identity and real target/native/remote comparisons.

Execution is same-host, greedy and eager, with draft TP1. Prefix caching, async scheduling, streaming input, LoRA and multimodal requests remain restricted for this backend. The native model implementations perform computation; this change supplies process placement and its state contract.

The intended benefit is target GPU memory relief and placement flexibility, following the [MTP offload question in the RFC](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42109#issuecomment-4561513801). Compare performance with native local MTP/EAGLE3 as well as target-only execution. Separate processes can add transfer and preparation latency, and a dedicated draft device increases total memory use. More available target KV does not by itself establish a larger supported context length. This increment does not implement the RFC's predictive fan-out cache or claim target/draft compute overlap.

AI assistance: Codex and Claude Code were used for implementation and testing. Human review of the final diff remains pending.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Run complete remote CPU suites and record the exact collected test cases."""
+
+import argparse
+import ast
+import json
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+NATIVE_SUITES = {
+    "test_gpu_runtime.py",
+    "test_mtp_contracts.py",
+    "test_remote_config.py",
+    "test_target_kv_runtime.py",
+    "test_token_gpu.py",
+}
+EXTERNAL_REGRESSIONS = {
+    "tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py": (
+        "test_worker_invalid_drafts_follow_queued_step_and_grammar_union",
+    ),
+    "tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_input_batch_v2.py": (
+        "test_model_input_padding_preserves_logical_tokens",
+        "test_invalid_spec_tokens_use_current_packed_request_boundaries",
+    ),
+    "tests/v1/test_serial_utils.py": (
+        "test_model_runner_invalid_draft_metadata_round_trip",
+    ),
+}
+
+
+def regression_nodes(suite: str = "all", root: Path = Path(".")) -> list[str]:
+    tests = root / "tests/v1/spec_decode/remote"
+    nodes = [
+        str(path.relative_to(root))
+        for path in sorted(tests.glob("test_*.py"))
+        if suite == "all" or (path.name in NATIVE_SUITES) == (suite == "native")
+    ]
+    if suite != "native":
+        nodes.append(".github/workflows/scripts/test_remote_cpu_regressions.py")
+    if suite != "control":
+        for name, candidates in EXTERNAL_REGRESSIONS.items():
+            path = root / name
+            if path.is_file():
+                definitions = {
+                    node.name
+                    for node in ast.parse(path.read_text()).body
+                    if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef)
+                }
+                nodes.extend(
+                    f"{name}::{test}" for test in candidates if test in definitions
+                )
+    return nodes
+
+
+class CollectionReport:
+    def __init__(self, path: Path, nodes: list[str], suite: str):
+        self.path = path
+        self.report = {
+            "suite": suite,
+            "revision": subprocess.check_output(
+                ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], text=True
+            ).strip(),
+            "selected": nodes,
+            "collected": [],
+            "collected_count": 0,
+            "outcomes": {},
+        }
+        self.write()
+
+    def write(self):
+        self.path.write_text(json.dumps(self.report, indent=2) + "\n")
+
+    def pytest_collection_finish(self, session):
+        self.report["collected"] = [item.nodeid for item in session.items]
+        self.report["collected_count"] = len(session.items)
+        self.write()
+
+    def pytest_runtest_logreport(self, report):
+        if report.when == "call" or report.failed or report.skipped:
+            self.report["outcomes"][report.nodeid] = report.outcome
+
+    def pytest_sessionfinish(self, session, exitstatus):
+        self.report["exitstatus"] = int(exitstatus)
+        self.write()
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--list", action="store_true", help="Print selected pytest nodes"
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--suite", choices=("all", "control", "native"), default="all")
+    parser.add_argument("--artifacts", type=Path, default=Path("remote-cpu-results"))
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    nodes = regression_nodes(args.suite)
+    if args.list:
+        print("\n".join(nodes))
+        return 0
+
+    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd()))
+    import pytest
+
+    args.artifacts.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    report = CollectionReport(args.artifacts / "collection.json", nodes, args.suite)
+    if not nodes:
+        print(f"No {args.suite} suites exist on this branch.")
+        return 0
+    return int(
+        pytest.main(
+            [
+                "--noconftest",
+                "-p",
+                "pytest_timeout",
+                "--timeout=60",
+                "-q",
+                f"--junitxml={args.artifacts / 'junit.xml'}",
+                *nodes,
+            ],
+            plugins=[report],
+        )
+    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+# Remote draft placement (experimental)
+
+Remote placement separates a target-conditioned speculator from the target
+process. The target remains responsible for verification and sampling. Placement
+is configured independently of the speculative method; native local execution
+remains the default.
+
+The standalone GPU runtime provides same-host target-conditioned execution with
+independent draft KV. It supports greedy, eager MRV2 execution, target TP1 or TP2
+and draft TP1. The protocol test adapter is for development only.
+
+## Configuration and lifecycle
+
+`speculative_config.remote_draft` takes a single `endpoint`, a `transport`
+(`auto` or `inline`) and a `failure_policy` (`target_only` or `error`). `auto`
+selects inline. Use a Unix socket or loopback TCP endpoint on the same host.
+The protocol does not authenticate peers; non-loopback server binding requires
+explicit `--allow-remote-connections`.
+
+The default request budget is 100 ms and the initial connection budget is
+30,000 ms. A request timeout under `target_only` permanently disables remote
+speculation for affected requests, returning zero valid drafts while the target
+continues. `error` surfaces the failure. Reconnection may admit new identities;
+it does not rebuild the old requests' draft KV. Generation and session fencing
+prevent late replies from reactivating retired state. Replies for another session,
+request, or batch are discarded before their ordering counters or draft tokens are
+used.
+
+Protocol v2.2 assigns one server execution deadline to each pipelined prefill
+group. Waiting behind an earlier chunk consumes that group's remaining budget.
+With older peers, the client waits for each prefill ACK before sending the next
+chunk, using the same round deadline. Already executing GPU work is not cancelled.
+When buffered final prompt chunks require multiple draft forwards, they also
+share the proposal deadline; expired rows do not start another forward.
+
+Socket cleanup errors encountered while handling a transport failure do not
+replace that failure or interrupt the configured fallback.
+
+Feature schema and frame byte budgets are checked before tensor serialization.
+Connections, partial frames, pending bytes and adapter waiters have server-side
+bounds. A shutdown grace timeout does not authorize freeing GPU storage whose
+completion is unknown; the process must be restarted in that state.
+
+This placement does not provide predictive caching, cross-node execution or
+N:M routing. Moving a speculator to another GPU does not by itself overlap its
+computation with target verification or guarantee higher throughput.
+
+## Standalone GPU example
+
+For MiMo-7B-RL MTP K=1, start the draft process on its assigned GPU:
+
+```bash
+VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python -m vllm.v1.spec_decode.remote.server \
+  --adapter gpu --endpoint unix:///tmp/vllm-draft.sock --device cuda:1 \
+  --target-model XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-7B-RL --draft-model XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-7B-RL \
+  --method mtp --num-speculative-tokens 1 --dtype bfloat16 \
+  --max-batch-size 8 --max-model-len 4096 --max-feature-tokens 512 \
+  --draft-kv-cache-gib 1 --block-size 16 --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN \
+  --target-attention-backend FLASH_ATTN
+```
+
+Use immutable target/draft revisions for reproducible evaluations. The server
+loads and warms its actual prefill/decode path before listening. Required shared
+weights are validated without loading the target transformer stack.
+
+Configure the target on GPU 0 with the matching model, revisions and limits:
+
+```python
+from vllm import LLM
+
+llm = LLM(
+    model="XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-7B-RL",
+    max_model_len=4096,
+    max_num_seqs=8,
+    max_num_batched_tokens=512,
+    enable_prefix_caching=False,
+    async_scheduling=False,
+    enforce_eager=True,
+    attention_config={"backend": "FLASH_ATTN"},
+    speculative_config={
+        "method": "mtp",
+        "num_speculative_tokens": 1,
+        "draft_sample_method": "greedy",
+        "attention_backend": "FLASH_ATTN",
+        "remote_draft": {
+            "endpoint": "unix:///tmp/vllm-draft.sock",
+            "transport": "inline",
+            "request_timeout_ms": 5000,
+            "failure_policy": "error",
+        },
+    },
+)
+```
+
+Set `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` for the target too. Both processes must agree on
+target/draft device assignments and checkpoint/schema identities. The example's
+5000 ms budget is explicit; it does not establish that the 100 ms default is
+suitable for long prefills. EAGLE3 currently accepts GPT-OSS and Qwen3 targets;
+see [own-KV MTP contracts](remote_mtp.md) for the experimental MTP families.
+Prefix caching, input streaming, async scheduling, multimodal input, LoRA and
+`draft_lm_head_quantization` are rejected for this backend. Native local speculation retains its own support.

@@ -0,0 +1,112 @@
+# Standalone own-KV MTP
+
+The experimental standalone runtime can place a target-conditioned MTP head in
+another process. It uses the native MRV2 MTP forward path and transports target
+hidden states. The target still verifies every proposed token. This placement
+can reduce target GPU memory use; it does not imply faster decoding or overlap
+between target and draft computation.
+
+## Model contracts
+
+The runtime checks the resolved draft architecture and its matching target,
+including hidden width, vocabulary size and the number of checkpoint MTP modules.
+It currently requires exactly one MTP module and scalar token positions.
+
+| Resolved draft architecture | Matching target | Draft cache | K restriction |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `MiMoMTPModel` | `MiMoForCausalLM` | Full attention | 1 |
+| `ErnieMTPModel` | `Ernie4_5_MoeForCausalLM` | Full attention | 1 |
+| `Qwen3NextMTP` | `Qwen3NextForCausalLM` | Full attention | Native sequential rollout |
+| `Glm4MoeMTPModel` | `Glm4MoeForCausalLM` | Full attention | Native sequential rollout |
+| `Glm4MoeLiteMTPModel` | `Glm4MoeLiteForCausalLM` | Dense MLA | Native sequential rollout |
+| `ExaoneMoeMTP` | `ExaoneMoeForCausalLM` / `ExaoneMoEForCausalLM` | Uniform full attention or sliding window | Native sequential rollout |
+| `NemotronHMTPModel` | `NemotronHForCausalLM` / `NemotronHPuzzleForCausalLM` | Attention/MoE-only MTP block | Native sequential rollout |
+| `HYV3MTPModel` | `HYV3ForCausalLM` | Full attention | Native sequential rollout |
+
+These are explicit implementation contracts, not validation of every checkpoint
+or topology in each family. A target with hybrid attention or recurrent layers
+can have a conventional attention-only MTP head. The target's architecture name
+alone does not determine the draft's cache layout.
+
+The draft's effective `max_model_len`, derived from its own checkpoint position
+settings and any speculative context limit, must cover the target's configured
+`max_model_len`. Startup rejects shorter drafts before native execution. Reduce
+the target context limit to use such a checkpoint. Setting a round's K to zero
+does not bypass this requirement: MTP still updates draft context in that round.
+
+Exaone MTP modules use the draft checkpoint's module count, attention types and
+sliding windows, including when the draft checkpoint is published separately
+from the target.
+
+HYV3 and ERNIE MTP heads use the selected draft checkpoint's normalization,
+rotary position settings and module layout, including when the draft checkpoint
+is published separately from the target.
+
+Native unquantized HYV3 loading checks every MTP-owned parameter, including each
+packed projection and local expert shard. Draft-only checkpoints may omit the
+target-owned embedding and LM head; the native proposer installs them after
+loading. Included tied heads load from the checkpoint embedding, and included
+untied heads load from its LM head. An explicit native loader
+`enable_weights_track=False` retains the existing unchecked-loading opt-out.
+
+The standalone allocator accepts one homogeneous, unquantized full-attention,
+dense MLA, or sliding-window group. It uses the shared vLLM KV allocator and
+retains a null block. Sliding-window attention conservatively reserves the full
+context; the attention backend applies the window, and this runtime does not
+recycle evicted window pages. Budget the draft KV accordingly.
+
+Sparse/indexer MLA (including any `index_topk` configuration), compressed or
+packed KV, mixed KV groups, multiple MTP modules, multimodal features, mRoPE and
+mHC are rejected. Nemotron MTP must contain only attention and MoE layers.
+Gemma4's Q-only assistant reads target-owned KV and is not supported by this
+own-KV adapter. Its native local path is unaffected.
+
+## Shared weights and execution
+
+The standalone process loads the target embedding and LM head without loading
+its transformer layers. Automatic checkpoint downloads use the resolved target
+revision. Nemotron embedding names follow its native loader: `model` or
+`backbone` prefixes with `embeddings` or `embed_tokens`. Exactly one matching
+tensor must be present. Ambiguous aliases, incompatible shapes and quantized
+embedding/head tensors are rejected instead of being interpreted as ordinary
+floating-point weights.
+
+Remote checkpoint identity uses a resolved immutable Hugging Face commit, or
+SHA-256 digests of local checkpoint artifacts and shard indexes. Local directories
+are identified by their contents rather than their deployment path. These files
+are streamed once per contract construction at startup; hashing adds startup I/O,
+not a per-round cost. Checkpoints must remain unchanged between contract creation
+and model loading, and throughout serving; hot reload is unsupported. Local
+tokenizer artifacts are likewise hashed independently of their directory path.
+
+An alternate `--shared-weights-source` must be a local directory. Its selected
+embedding and head tensors must match the target checkpoint in dtype, shape and
+contents before GPU materialization. Unpinned alternate repositories and shape-
+compatible replacement weights are rejected; this option stages identical shared
+weights rather than changing the model being advertised by the handshake.
+
+The runtime remains greedy, eager, same-host and draft TP1. Existing remote
+restrictions on target topology, prefix caching, asynchronous scheduling,
+resumable input, multimodal inputs and LoRA still apply. Native local MTP does
+not inherit these placement restrictions. Set attention backends supported by
+the actual draft layout: dense MLA requires an MLA backend; a full-attention
+backend used by another checkpoint is not interchangeable.
+
+Remote drafting also rejects KV consumer connectors and KV offloading, including
+consumer children of a `MultiConnector`. External KV hits skip target prefill
+even when prefix caching is disabled, leaving the remote drafter without the
+context it requires. Producer-only connectors retain their existing validation.
+
+## Validation boundaries
+
+CPU tests cover real Transformers configuration normalization, architecture and
+feature rejection, shared-weight selection, and the real KV allocator. The KV
+tests check independent layer/block writes, dense MLA latent storage and kernel
+block splitting, sliding-window rejection/cleanup, and exact budget boundaries.
+These tests do not establish attention numerics or model output correctness.
+
+Model validation must record the exact source and checkpoint revisions, compare
+native and remote output, require nonzero proposed and accepted drafts, and
+check cleanup. Same-GPU tests exercise process separation but do not measure
+cross-GPU transport or memory savings. A checkpoint without recorded model
+validation remains experimental even when its configuration passes the contract.

+@contextmanager
+def draft_server(
+    model: str,
+    log_path: Path,
+    *,
+    revision: str | None = REVISION,
+    num_speculative_tokens: int = 1,
+    attention_backend: str = "FLASH_ATTN",
+    draft_kv_cache_gib: float = 0.25,
+    max_feature_tokens: int = 64,
+    trust_remote_code: bool = True,
+    moe_backend: str | None = None,
+    on_ready: Callable[[subprocess.Popen], None] | None = None,
+):
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="vllm-remote-") as directory:
+        path = Path(directory) / "draft.sock"
+        command = [
+            sys.executable,
+            "-m",
+            "vllm.v1.spec_decode.remote.server",
+            "--adapter",
+            "gpu",
+            "--endpoint",
+            f"unix://{path}",
+            "--target-model",
+            model,
+            "--draft-model",
+            model,
+            "--method",
+            "mtp",
+            "--num-speculative-tokens",
+            str(num_speculative_tokens),
+            "--device",
+            "cuda:0",
+            "--dtype",
+            "bfloat16",
+            "--max-batch-size",
+            "4",
+            "--max-model-len",
+            "128",
+            "--max-feature-tokens",
+            str(max_feature_tokens),
+            "--draft-kv-cache-gib",
+            str(draft_kv_cache_gib),
+            "--block-size",
+            "16",
+            "--attention-backend",
+            attention_backend,
+            "--target-attention-backend",
+            attention_backend,
+        ]
+        if trust_remote_code:
+            command.append("--trust-remote-code")
+        if moe_backend is not None:
+            command.extend(["--moe-backend", moe_backend])
+        if revision is not None:
+            command.extend(
+                ["--target-revision", revision, "--draft-revision", revision]
+            )
+        with log_path.open("w") as log:
+            process = subprocess.Popen(
+                command, stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, start_new_session=True
+            )
+            try:
+                deadline = time.monotonic() + 600
+                while True:
+                    if process.poll() is not None:
+                        pytest.fail(
+                            f"draft server exited {process.returncode}: {log_path}"
+                        )
+                    with socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX) as probe:
+                        if probe.connect_ex(str(path)) == 0:
+                            break
+                    if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
+                        pytest.fail(
+                            f"draft server did not listen after warmup: {log_path}"
+                        )
+                    time.sleep(0.1)
+                if on_ready is not None:
+                    on_ready(process)
+                yield f"unix://{path}"
+            finally:
+                if process.poll() is None:
+                    os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGINT)
+                    try:
+                        process.wait(timeout=30)
+                    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+                        os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+                        process.wait(timeout=5)
+                        pytest.fail(f"draft server did not shut down: {log_path}")
+                assert process.returncode == 0, f"draft server failed: {log_path}"
+

+@contextmanager
+def paused_draft_server(process: subprocess.Popen):
+    """Stop an owned draft process until the caller finishes its timeout check."""
+    try:
+        process.send_signal(signal.SIGSTOP)
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + 5
+        while True:
+            stopped = os.waitid(os.P_PID, process.pid, os.WSTOPPED | os.WNOHANG)
+            if stopped is not None:
+                assert stopped.si_status == signal.SIGSTOP
+                break
+            assert process.poll() is None, "draft server exited before stopping"
+            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
+                pytest.fail("draft server did not stop")
+            time.sleep(0.01)
+        yield
+    finally:
+        if process.poll() is None:
+            process.send_signal(signal.SIGCONT)

+def _unpack_mtp_experts(state):
+    """Preserve packed HF expert values under native per-expert checkpoint names."""
+    import torch
+
+    weights = {}
+    for name, tensor in state.items():
+        if name.endswith(".experts.gate_up_proj"):
+            prefix = name.removesuffix(".gate_up_proj")
+            gates, ups = tensor.chunk(2, dim=1)
+            for expert in range(tensor.shape[0]):
+                weights[f"{prefix}.{expert}.gate_proj.weight"] = gates[expert].clone()
+                weights[f"{prefix}.{expert}.up_proj.weight"] = ups[expert].clone()
+            reconstructed = torch.stack(
+                [
+                    torch.cat(
+                        (
+                            weights[f"{prefix}.{e}.gate_proj.weight"],
+                            weights[f"{prefix}.{e}.up_proj.weight"],
+                        )
+                    )
+                    for e in range(tensor.shape[0])
+                ]
+            )
+            assert torch.equal(reconstructed, tensor)
+        elif name.endswith((".experts.up_proj", ".experts.down_proj")):
+            prefix, projection = name.rsplit(".", 1)
+            for expert in range(tensor.shape[0]):
+                weights[f"{prefix}.{expert}.{projection}.weight"] = tensor[
+                    expert
+                ].clone()
+            assert torch.equal(
+                torch.stack(
+                    [
+                        weights[f"{prefix}.{e}.{projection}.weight"]
+                        for e in range(tensor.shape[0])
+                    ]
+                ),
+                tensor,
+            )
+        else:
+            weights[name] = tensor.clone()
+    return weights

+def _save_mtp_checkpoint(path, config, weights):
+    import torch
+    from safetensors.torch import load_file, save_file
+    from tokenizers import Tokenizer, models, pre_tokenizers
+    from transformers import TokenizersBackend
+
+    for name, tensor in weights.items():
+        dtype = (
+            torch.float32
+            if name.endswith(
+                (
+                    ".gate.weight",
+                    ".e_score_correction_bias",
+                    ".expert_bias",
+                    ".A_log",
+                    ".dt_bias",
+                    ".D",
+                )
+            )
+            else torch.bfloat16
+        )
+        weights[name] = tensor.to(dtype).contiguous()
+        assert torch.isfinite(weights[name]).all()
+    path.mkdir()
+    save_file(weights, path / "model.safetensors", metadata={"format": "pt"})
+    reloaded = load_file(path / "model.safetensors")
+    assert weights.keys() == reloaded.keys()
+    assert all(torch.equal(tensor, reloaded[name]) for name, tensor in weights.items())
+    config.save_pretrained(path)
+    vocabulary = {token: i for i, token in enumerate(("<pad>", "<s>", "</s>", "<unk>"))}
+    vocabulary.update({f"t{i}": i for i in range(4, 128)})
+    backend = Tokenizer(models.WordLevel(vocabulary, unk_token="<unk>"))
+    backend.pre_tokenizer = pre_tokenizers.Whitespace()
+    tokenizer = TokenizersBackend(
+        tokenizer_object=backend,
+        pad_token="<pad>",
+        bos_token="<s>",
+        eos_token="</s>",
+        unk_token="<unk>",
+        model_max_length=128,
+    )

+    if moe_backend is not None:

+    if hybrid_target:
+        kwargs.update(mamba_backend="triton", use_replayssm=False)
+    if mtp_family == "qwen3_next":
+        kwargs["gdn_prefill_backend"] = "triton"
+        monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_GDN_DECODE_KERNEL", "triton")
+    prompts = [
+        {"prompt_token_ids": [3 + (i * 7) % 125 for i in range(length)]}
+        for length in (15, 16, 17, 31, 32, 33, 65)
+    ]
+    batches = (
+        prompts[:1],
+        [prompts[i] for i in (4, 1, 6, 2)],

+    record_property(

+            mismatches += sum(

+                for output, expected_output in zip(outputs, expected_outputs)
+                for token, expected_token in zip(output[0], expected_output[0])

+def _separate_mtp_draft(source, destination):
+    """Keep real checkpoint weights while changing the draft's scalar settings."""
+    import json
+    import shutil
+
+    shutil.copytree(source, destination, copy_function=os.link)
+    path = destination / "config.json"
+    config = json.loads(path.read_text())
+    config["rms_norm_eps"] = 0.001
+    config["rope_parameters"]["rope_theta"] *= 2
+    path.unlink()
+    path.write_text(json.dumps(config))
+    return str(destination)

+def make_planner(num_blocks=64, max_num_reqs=4, max_model_len=64):
+    return DraftStepPlanner(
+        DraftBlockPool(num_blocks, BLOCK_SIZE),
+        max_num_reqs=max_num_reqs,
+        max_model_len=max_model_len,
+        num_speculative_tokens=K,
+    )
+
+
+def digest_row(prefix, next_token) -> list[int]:
+    digest = sum((token + 1) * (position + 1) for position, token in enumerate(prefix))
+    return [(digest + next_token + j) % VOCAB for j in range(K)]
+
+
+class KVDigestExecutor(DraftStepExecutor):
+    """Deterministic external CPU executor with actual per-request KV storage.
+
+    Writes (position, target token) into every token's KV slot and drafts
+    from a digest of the committed prefix read back through its own block
+    tables, so any position, slot, block table, or committed-length error
+    in the runtime changes the drafts.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, pool: DraftBlockPool, max_num_tokens=None):
+        self.pool = pool
+        self._max_num_tokens = max_num_tokens
+        self.kv = np.full(pool.num_blocks * pool.block_size, -1, dtype=np.int64)
+        self.block_tables: dict[int, list[int]] = defaultdict(list)
+        self.plans: list[DraftStepPlan] = []
+        self.effective_ks: list[int] = []
+
+    @property
+    def max_num_tokens(self):
+        return self._max_num_tokens
+
+    def execute(self, plan, features, *, num_speculative_tokens=None):
+        effective_k = K if num_speculative_tokens is None else num_speculative_tokens
+        self.effective_ks.append(effective_k)
+        if self.max_num_tokens is not None and plan.num_tokens > self.max_num_tokens:
+            raise ValueError("draft step exceeds the configured feature-token budget")
+        self.plans.append(plan)
+        for req_index, update in plan.block_table_updates.items():
+            table = self.block_tables[req_index][: update.start]
+            self.block_tables[req_index] = table + update.block_ids
+        tokens = features[0].numpy().astype(np.int64)
+        assert tokens.shape == (plan.num_tokens,)
+        self.kv[plan.slot_mapping] = plan.positions * STRIDE + tokens
+        drafts = []
+        for i in range(plan.num_reqs):
+            committed = int(plan.seq_lens[i] - plan.num_rejected[i])
+            table = np.array(self.block_tables[int(plan.req_indices[i])])
+            positions = np.arange(committed)
+            slots = table[positions // BLOCK_SIZE] * BLOCK_SIZE + positions % BLOCK_SIZE
+            values = self.kv[slots]
+            assert (values // STRIDE == positions).all()
+            next_token = (
+                plan.last_sampled[i]
+                if plan.num_sampled[i]
+                else plan.next_prefill_tokens[i][0]
+            )
+            drafts.append(
+                digest_row((values % STRIDE).tolist(), int(next_token))[:effective_k]
+                + [0] * (K - effective_k)
+            )
+        return torch.tensor(drafts)

+"""Classify allocation failures once, independently of server lifecycle stages."""
+
+import errno
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.v1.spec_decode.remote.errors import (
+    CompletionUnknownError,
+    CudaRuntimeError,
+    cuda_context_fatal,
+    host_allocation_failure,
+    runtime_unusable,
+)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "error,fatal,unusable,host_oom",
+    [
+        (MemoryError("allocation failed"), False, False, True),
+        (OSError(errno.ENOMEM, "allocation failed"), False, False, True),
+        (
+            RuntimeError(
+                "[enforce fail at alloc_cpu.cpp:127] err == 0. "
+                "DefaultCPUAllocator: can't allocate memory: you tried to allocate "
+                "67108864 bytes. Error code 12 (Cannot allocate memory)"
+            ),
+            False,
+            False,
+            True,
+        ),
+        (torch.OutOfMemoryError("CUDA out of memory"), False, False, False),
+        (RuntimeError("ordinary adapter failure"), False, False, False),
+        (OSError(errno.EINVAL, "invalid allocation argument"), False, False, False),
+        (
+            RuntimeError(
+                "DefaultCPUAllocator: can't allocate memory: you tried to allocate "
+                "64 bytes. Error code 22 (Invalid argument)"
+            ),
+            False,
+            False,
+            False,
+        ),
+        (CudaRuntimeError("allocation failed", cuda_error_code=2), False, False, False),
+        (CompletionUnknownError("upload completion unknown"), False, True, False),
+        *[
+            (RuntimeError(detail), True, True, False)
+            for detail in (
+                "CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered",
+                "CUDA error: device-side assert triggered",
+                "CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS",
+                "cudaEventQuery failed: hardware stack error (714)",
+                "cudaErrorHardwareStackError",
+                "CUDA error: tensor memory not completely freed",
+                "CUDA_ERROR_TENSOR_MEMORY_LEAK",
+                "cudaErrorContained",
+                "cudaErrorMpsClientTerminated",
+            )
+        ],
+        *[
+            (
+                CudaRuntimeError("opaque failure", cuda_error_code=code),
+                True,
+                True,
+                False,
+            )
+            for code in (226, 700, 702, 710, 714, 715, 716, 717, 718, 719, 810)
+        ],
+    ],
+)
+def test_error_classification(error, fatal, unusable, host_oom):
+    assert cuda_context_fatal(error) is fatal
+    assert runtime_unusable(error) is unusable
+    assert host_allocation_failure(error) is host_oom
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("wrapper", [MemoryError, torch.OutOfMemoryError, RuntimeError])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("link", ["cause", "context"])
+def test_fatal_chain_takes_precedence_over_allocation_error(wrapper, link):
+    error = wrapper("allocation after CUDA failure")
+    fatal = RuntimeError("CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered")
+    if link == "cause":
+        error.__cause__ = fatal
+    else:
+        error.__context__ = fatal
+        error.__cause__ = ValueError("nonfatal explicit cause")
+    assert cuda_context_fatal(error)
+    assert runtime_unusable(error)
+    assert not host_allocation_failure(error)
+
+
+def test_prior_host_allocation_does_not_mask_a_new_unrelated_error():
+    error = ValueError("invalid shape")
+    error.__cause__ = MemoryError("prior allocation failure")
+    assert not host_allocation_failure(error)
+    assert not runtime_unusable(error)
+
+
+def test_completion_unknown_survives_wrapping_and_exception_cycles():
+    uncertain = CompletionUnknownError("copy did not complete")
+    wrapper = RuntimeError("feature import failed")
+    wrapper.__context__ = uncertain
+    uncertain.__cause__ = wrapper
+    assert runtime_unusable(wrapper)
+    assert not cuda_context_fatal(wrapper)
+    assert not host_allocation_failure(wrapper)

+def _spec(kind):
+    kwargs = dict(
+        block_size=4,
+        num_kv_heads=2,
+        head_size=3,
+        dtype=torch.float32 if kind == "full" else torch.bfloat16,
+    )
+    if kind == "mla":
+        return MLAAttentionSpec(**(kwargs | {"num_kv_heads": 1, "head_size": 5}))
+    if kind == "swa":
+        return SlidingWindowSpec(**kwargs, head_size_v=4, sliding_window=5)
+    return FullAttentionSpec(**kwargs)

+def test_dense_own_kv_layers_and_blocks_never_alias(kind, layout_name):
+    spec = _spec(kind)
+    names = ["draft.0", "draft.1", "draft.2"]
+    assert select_standalone_kv_spec(dict.fromkeys(names, spec)) is spec
+    page_group_bytes = len(names) * spec.page_size_bytes
+    budget = page_group_bytes * 6 - 1
+    layout = KVCacheLayout[layout_name]
+    config = make_standalone_kv_config(spec, names, budget, layout)
+    caches = allocate_kv_cache(config, torch.device("cpu"), layout)
+    assert config.num_blocks == 5
+    assert config.kv_cache_groups[0].kv_cache_spec is spec
+    for layer, cache in enumerate(caches.values()):
+        assert cache.shape == (
+            5,
+            spec.num_kv_heads,
+            4,
+            spec.head_size + spec.head_size_v,
+        )
+        assert cache.untyped_storage().nbytes() == page_group_bytes * 5
+        for block in range(1, 5):
+            cache[block].fill_(10 * layer + block)
+    for layer, cache in enumerate(caches.values()):
+        assert not cache[0].count_nonzero().item()
+        for block in range(1, 5):
+            assert torch.all(cache[block] == 10 * layer + block)
+    assert len({cache.untyped_storage().data_ptr() for cache in caches.values()}) == 1
+    assert page_group_bytes * 5 <= budget

+def chunk(tokens, lookahead=None):
+    return FeatureBatch(
+        1,
+        (
+            torch.tensor(tokens, dtype=torch.int32),
+            None
+            if lookahead is None
+            else torch.tensor([[lookahead]], dtype=torch.int32),
+        ),
+    )

+def round_(
+    session,
+    batch_id,
+    keys,
+    query_lens,
+    tokens,
+    accepted,
+    recovery,
+    *,
+    num_speculative_tokens=None,
+):
+    return session.collect(
+        session.dispatch(
+            RemoteProposalBatch(
+                batch_id=batch_id,
+                keys=tuple(keys),
+                accepted_counts=torch.tensor(accepted, dtype=torch.int32),
+                recovery_tokens=torch.tensor(recovery, dtype=torch.int64),
+                features=chunk(tokens),
+                query_lens=torch.tensor(query_lens, dtype=torch.int32),
+                num_speculative_tokens=num_speculative_tokens,
+            )
+        )
+    )

+    b = session.open_sequence(2)
+    session.prefill_many([(a, chunk([14, 15]), True), (b, chunk([21, 22]), True)])

+    result = round_(session, 0, [a, b], [0, 0], [], [0, 0], [30, 40])

+    b_drafts = digest_row([21, 22], 40)
+    assert result.row_statuses == (OK, OK)

+    # a accepts two drafts, b none; rejected positions must not leak into

+def checksum(*frames) -> int:
+    value = 0
+    for frame in frames:
+        value = zlib.crc32(frame.payload, value)
+    return value & 0x7FFFFFFF

+class RawClient:
+    """Minimal verifier that speaks the protocol directly."""
+
+    def __init__(self, endpoint: str):
+        self.conn = connect(endpoint, timeout=5.0)
+        self.session_id = ""
+        self.request_id = 0
+        self.frames: dict[int, DataFrame] = {}
+        self.next_slot = 100
+
+    def send(self, message, *, frames=()):
+        for frame in frames:
+            self.conn.send_data(frame)
+        self.request_id += 1
+        self.conn.send_control(
+            encode_message(
+                message, session_id=self.session_id, request_id=self.request_id
+            )
+        )
+        return self.request_id
+
+    def recv(self, timeout: float = 5.0):
+        while True:
+            frame = self.conn.recv(timeout=timeout)
+            if frame.kind == FRAME_DATA:
+                data = decode_data_frame(frame.body)
+                self.frames[data.slot] = data
+                continue
+            envelope = decode_envelope(frame.body)
+            return envelope, decode_payload(envelope)
+
+    def call(self, message, *, frames=()):
+        request_id = self.send(message, frames=frames)
+        envelope, reply = self.recv()
+        assert envelope.request_id == request_id
+        return reply
+
+    def hello(self, **overrides) -> HelloAck:
+        fields = dict(
+            verifier_instance_id=VERIFIER,
+            target_fingerprint="tf",
+            tokenizer_fingerprint="kf",
+            method="eagle3",
+            num_speculative_tokens=NUM_SPEC_TOKENS,
+            parallel_drafting=False,
+            supported_transports=("inline",),
+        )
+        fields.update(overrides)
+        reply = self.call(Hello(**fields))
+        if isinstance(reply, HelloAck):
+            self.session_id = reply.session_id
+        return reply
+
+    def open(self, k: SequenceKey) -> SequenceAck:
+        return self.call(OpenSequence(key=k))
+
+    def prefill(
+        self,
+        k: SequenceKey,
+        tokens,
+        *,
+        offset: int,
+        is_final=True,
+        checksum_override=None,
+    ) -> SequenceAck:
+        slot = self.reserve(1)
+        frame = ints_to_frame(slot, tokens)
+        chunk = PrefillChunk(
+            key=k,
+            offset=offset,
+            num_tokens=len(tokens),
+            is_final=is_final,
+            feature_slot=slot,
+            checksum=checksum(frame)
+            if checksum_override is None
+            else checksum_override,
+        )
+        return self.call(chunk, frames=[frame])
+
+    def ready(self, k: SequenceKey, tokens=(1, 2, 3)) -> None:
+        assert self.open(k).status is OK
+        assert self.prefill(k, list(tokens), offset=0).status is OK
+
+    def propose(
+        self,
+        batch_id: int,
+        keys,
+        recovery,
+        accepted=None,
+        *,
+        num_speculative_tokens=None,
+    ):
+        accepted = accepted or [0] * len(keys)
+        base = self.reserve(3)
+        frames = [
+            ints_to_frame(base, accepted),
+            ints_to_frame(base + 1, recovery),
+            ints_to_frame(base + 2, recovery),
+        ]
+        message = AdvanceAndPropose(
+            batch_id=batch_id,
+            keys=tuple(keys),
+            accepted_counts_slot=base,
+            recovery_tokens_slot=base + 1,
+            feature_slot=base + 2,
+            num_speculative_tokens=num_speculative_tokens,
+        )
+        return self.call(message, frames=frames)
+
+    def propose_with_frames(self, batch_id, keys, accepted, recovery, feature):
+        base = self.reserve(3)
+        frames = [
+            DataFrame(base, accepted.dtype, accepted.shape, accepted.payload),
+            DataFrame(base + 1, recovery.dtype, recovery.shape, recovery.payload),
+            DataFrame(base + 2, feature.dtype, feature.shape, feature.payload),
+        ]
+        return self.call(
+            AdvanceAndPropose(
+                batch_id=batch_id,
+                keys=tuple(keys),
+                accepted_counts_slot=base,
+                recovery_tokens_slot=base + 1,
+                feature_slot=base + 2,
+            ),
+            frames=frames,
+        )
+
+    def propose_ragged(self, batch_id, keys, query_lens, token_ids, *, lens=True):
+        base = self.reserve(4)
+        frames = [
+            ints_to_frame(base, [0] * len(keys)),
+            ints_to_frame(base + 1, [1] * len(keys)),
+            ints_to_frame(base + 3, token_ids),
+        ]
+        if lens:
+            frames.append(ints_to_frame(base + 2, query_lens))
+        return self.call(
+            AdvanceAndPropose(
+                batch_id=batch_id,
+                keys=tuple(keys),
+                accepted_counts_slot=base,
+                recovery_tokens_slot=base + 1,
+                feature_slot=base + 3,
+                query_lens_slot=base + 2,
+            ),
+            frames=frames,
+        )
+
+    def result(self, response: ProposalResponse):
+        base = response.result_slot
+        assert base is not None
+        tokens = self.frames.pop(base)
+        valid = self.frames.pop(base + 1)
+        statuses = self.frames.pop(base + 2)
+        rows = tokens.shape[0]
+        flat = frame_to_ints(tokens)
+        return (
+            [
+                flat[i * NUM_SPEC_TOKENS : (i + 1) * NUM_SPEC_TOKENS]
+                for i in range(rows)
+            ],
+            frame_to_ints(valid),
+            [SpeculatorStatusCode(s) for s in frame_to_ints(statuses)],
+        )
+
+    def reserve(self, count: int) -> int:
+        slot = self.next_slot
+        self.next_slot += count
+        return slot
+
+    def close(self):
+        self.conn.close()
+

+            sending.set()
+            if not release.wait(timeout=5.0):
+                raise TimeoutError("error reply was not released")
+        return sendall(sock, data, *args, **kwargs)

+    monkeypatch.setattr(socket.socket, "sendall", slow_error_reply)

+    def reject():
+        try:
+            replies.append(
+                client.open(failed_key)
+                if failure == "queue_full"
+                else client.propose(
+                    0,
+                    [failed_key],
+                    recovery=[1],
+                    num_speculative_tokens=0 if failure == "draft_budget" else None,
+                )
+            )
+        except Exception as error:
+            errors.append(error)
+
+    def cleanup():
+        try:
+            reply = other.call(CloseSequence(keys=(other_key,)))
+            assert reply.status is OK
+            cleaned.set()
+        except Exception as error:
+            errors.append(error)
+
+    rejected = threading.Thread(target=reject)
+    closing = threading.Thread(target=cleanup)
+    try:
+        rejected.start()
+        assert sending.wait(timeout=5.0)
+        if failure != "queue_full":
+            assert server.registry.get(failed_key) is None
+            assert adapter.prefix(failed_key) is None
+        closing.start()
+        assert cleaned.wait(timeout=2.0)
+        assert server.registry.get(other_key) is None
+        assert adapter.prefix(other_key) is None
+    finally:
+        release.set()
+        rejected.join(timeout=5.0)
+        if closing.ident is not None:
+            closing.join(timeout=5.0)
+        other.close()
+    assert not rejected.is_alive() and not closing.is_alive()
+    assert not errors
+    expected = (
+        SpeculatorStatusCode.QUEUE_FULL
+        if failure == "queue_full"
+        else SpeculatorStatusCode.INTERNAL_ERROR

+                        limits=DEFAULT_LIMITS,
+                    ),
+                )
+                script(peer)
+            except BaseException as exc:
+                errors.append(exc)
+            finally:
+                for conn in connections:
+                    conn.close()
+
+        thread = threading.Thread(target=serve)
+        threads.append(thread)
+        thread.start()
+        return listener.endpoint
+
+    yield start
+    listener.close()
+    for conn in connections:
+        conn.close()
+    for thread in threads:
+        thread.join(timeout=5)
+        assert not thread.is_alive()

+def test_legacy_peer_does_not_receive_more_prefills_after_round_timeout(protocol_peer):
+    """Older peers cannot anchor pipelined commands to one execution budget."""
+    from vllm.v1.spec_decode.remote.protocol import Pong
+
+    def script(peer):
+        for _ in range(3):
+            envelope, opened, _ = peer.recv()
+            assert isinstance(opened, OpenSequence)
+            peer.reply(envelope, SequenceAck(opened.key))
+        _, first, _ = peer.recv()
+        assert isinstance(first, PrefillChunk)
+        # No first ACK: the shared client deadline must expire before another
+        # prefill can be sent. The next RPC flushes logical retirements.
+        envelope, closed, _ = peer.recv()
+        assert isinstance(closed, CloseSequence)
+        for key in closed.keys:
+            peer.reply(envelope, SequenceAck(key))
+        envelope, ping, _ = peer.recv()
+        assert isinstance(ping, Ping)
+        peer.reply(envelope, Pong(nonce=ping.nonce))
+
+    endpoint = protocol_peer(script, protocol_minor=1)
+    session = RemoteDraftSession(endpoint, IDENTITY, request_timeout_ms=200)
+    try:
+        session.connect()
+        first, second, _ = session.open_sequences((1, 2, 3))
+        session.prefill_many(
+            [(first, features([4]), False), (second, features([4]), False)]
+        )
+        assert session.sequence_state(first) is SequenceState.TARGET_ONLY
+        assert session.sequence_state(second) is SequenceState.TARGET_ONLY
+        assert session.ping().healthy
+    finally:
+        session.close()

+class PaddedAdapter(FakeDraftAdapter):
+    """Proposes one valid token per row and pads the rest with junk."""
+
+    def __init__(self, padding: int, first: int):
+        super().__init__(vocab_size=VOCAB)
+        self.padding = padding
+        self.first = first
+
+    def advance_and_propose(self, batch_):
+        result = super().advance_and_propose(batch_)
+        rows = len(batch_.keys)
+        row = [self.first] + [self.padding] * (NUM_SPEC_TOKENS - 1)
+        return dataclasses.replace(
+            result,
+            token_ids=tensor_to_frame(0, torch.tensor([row] * rows)),
+            valid_lengths=tensor_to_frame(0, torch.ones(rows, dtype=torch.int32)),
+        )
+

+def timeout_after_frames(monkeypatch, conn, completed_frames):
+    send_data = conn.send_data
+    sent = 0
+
+    def send(frame, *, deadline=None, drain_incoming=False):
+        nonlocal sent
+        if sent == completed_frames:
+            raise TransportTimeout("deadline elapsed before the next frame")
+        send_data(frame, deadline=deadline, drain_incoming=drain_incoming)
+        sent += 1
+
+    def reject_control(*args, **kwargs):
+        raise TransportTimeout("deadline elapsed before the control message")
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(conn, "send_data", send)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(conn, "send_control", reject_control)
+

+    send, wait = session._send, session._await
+    events = []
+    deadlines = []
+
+    def write(*args, **kwargs):
+        events.append("send")
+        deadlines.append(kwargs["deadline"])
+        result = send(*args, **kwargs)
+        clock.advance(0.02)
+        return result

+    def read(matches, ack_deadline, **kwargs):

+    monkeypatch.setattr(session, "_await", read)
+    keys = session.open_sequences((1, 2), deadline=deadline)
+    assert events == ["send", "send", "wait", "wait"]
+    assert deadlines == [deadline] * 4
+    assert keys[0].generation > previous.generation
+    assert keys[1].generation > keys[0].generation
+    assert session.sequence_state(previous) is None

+    cleaned = threading.Event()

+            cleaned.set()
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(adapter, "close_sequences", close_and_notify)
+    with monkeypatch.context() as patch:
+        if failure == "record":
+            make_record = session_module._SequenceRecord
+
+            def allocate(key, state):
+                if key.sequence_id == 2:
+                    raise MemoryError("injected open allocation failure")
+                return make_record(key, state)
+
+            patch.setattr(session_module, "_SequenceRecord", allocate)
+        elif failure == "ownership":
+
+            class Records(dict):
+                def __setitem__(self, sequence_id, record):
+                    if sequence_id == 2:
+                        raise MemoryError("injected open allocation failure")
+                    super().__setitem__(sequence_id, record)
+
+            # Keep the failed dictionary visible after the patch context.
+            session._records = Records(session._records)
+        else:
+            open_many = session._open_many
+
+            def fail_after_open(*args, **kwargs):
+                open_many(*args, **kwargs)
+                raise MemoryError("injected open allocation failure")
+
+            patch.setattr(session, "_open_many", fail_after_open)
+        with pytest.raises(MemoryError, match="open allocation"):

+    assert session.sequence_state(sibling) is SequenceState.INVALID
+    assert not session._retiring

+    assert len(server.registry) == 0

+    next_generation = session._next_generation
+    session._records = dict(session._records)
+    session.connect()
+    session.close_sequences((sibling,))
+    fresh = session.open_sequences((1, 2))
+    assert fresh[0].generation >= next_generation > generation
+    assert fresh[1].generation > fresh[0].generation
+    session.close_sequences((stale,))
+    session.prefill_many([(key, features([1]), True) for key in fresh])

+"""Client-side lifecycle state machines: one-shot proposal handles and the
+recover/latch rules for remote sequences."""

+import pytest

+from vllm.v1.spec_decode.remote.state import (
+    HandleState,
+    InvalidStateTransition,
+    SequenceState,
+    can_transition_sequence,

+
+def _walk_handle(*states: HandleState) -> HandleState:
+    current = states[0]
+    for new in states[1:]:
+        current = transition_handle(current, new)
+    return current
+
+
+def _walk_sequence(*states: SequenceState) -> SequenceState:
+    current = states[0]
+    for new in states[1:]:
+        current = transition_sequence(current, new)
+    return current
+
+
+def test_handle_happy_path():
+    assert (
+        _walk_handle(
+            HandleState.CREATED,
+            HandleState.DISPATCHED,
+            HandleState.COMPLETED,
+            HandleState.COLLECTED,
+        )
+        is HandleState.COLLECTED
+    )
+
+
+def test_handle_cannot_skip_dispatch():
+    with pytest.raises(InvalidStateTransition):
+        transition_handle(HandleState.CREATED, HandleState.COLLECTED)
+
+
+def test_timed_out_handle_is_still_collected_once():
+    state = _walk_handle(
+        HandleState.CREATED, HandleState.DISPATCHED, HandleState.TIMED_OUT
+    )
+    assert transition_handle(state, HandleState.COLLECTED) is HandleState.COLLECTED
+    with pytest.raises(InvalidStateTransition):
+        transition_handle(HandleState.TIMED_OUT, HandleState.COMPLETED)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("terminal", [HandleState.CANCELLED, HandleState.COLLECTED])
+def test_terminal_handle_states_reject_everything(terminal):
+    for new in HandleState:
+        with pytest.raises(InvalidStateTransition):
+            transition_handle(terminal, new)
+
+
+def test_sequence_main_path():
+    assert (
+        _walk_sequence(
+            SequenceState.OPENING,
+            SequenceState.PREFILLING,
+            SequenceState.READY,
+            SequenceState.IN_FLIGHT,
+            SequenceState.READY,
+            SequenceState.CLOSING,
+            SequenceState.CLOSED,
+        )
+        is SequenceState.CLOSED
+    )
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "state",
+    [
+        SequenceState.OPENING,
+        SequenceState.PREFILLING,
+        SequenceState.READY,
+        SequenceState.IN_FLIGHT,
+        SequenceState.DESYNCED,
+    ],
+)
+def test_live_sequence_can_always_close_invalidate_or_latch(state):
+    for new in (
+        SequenceState.CLOSING,
+        SequenceState.INVALID,
+        SequenceState.TARGET_ONLY,
+    ):
+        assert can_transition_sequence(state, new)

+def test_target_only_is_latched_until_close():
+    # The MVP never resumes remote proposals for a latched request.
+    for new in (
+        SequenceState.READY,
+        SequenceState.PREFILLING,
+        SequenceState.IN_FLIGHT,
+        SequenceState.DESYNCED,
+    ):
+        assert not can_transition_sequence(SequenceState.TARGET_ONLY, new)
+    assert can_transition_sequence(SequenceState.TARGET_ONLY, SequenceState.CLOSING)
+
+
+def test_desynced_recovers_only_through_prefill():
+    assert can_transition_sequence(SequenceState.DESYNCED, SequenceState.PREFILLING)
+    for new in (SequenceState.READY, SequenceState.IN_FLIGHT):
+        with pytest.raises(InvalidStateTransition):
+            transition_sequence(SequenceState.DESYNCED, new)

+
+def test_invalid_requires_reopen():
+    assert can_transition_sequence(SequenceState.INVALID, SequenceState.OPENING)
+    assert can_transition_sequence(SequenceState.INVALID, SequenceState.CLOSING)
+    for new in (SequenceState.PREFILLING, SequenceState.READY):
+        assert not can_transition_sequence(SequenceState.INVALID, new)
+
+
+def test_closed_is_terminal():
+    for new in SequenceState:
+        assert not can_transition_sequence(SequenceState.CLOSED, new)

+def test_failed_connect_releases_socket_while_traceback_is_retained(
+    monkeypatch, tmp_path, failure, close_fails
+):
+    """Ownership transfers only after connection setup has completed."""
+    sockets, errors = [], []
+    listener = listen("tcp://127.0.0.1:0")
+
+    class FailingSocket(socket.socket):
+        def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
+            super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
+            sockets.append(self)
+
+        def connect(self, address):
+            if failure == "timeout":
+                raise TimeoutError("injected connect timeout")
+            return super().connect(address)
+
+        def setsockopt(self, *args):
+            if failure == "tune" and args[:2] == (
+                socket.IPPROTO_TCP,
+                socket.TCP_NODELAY,
+            ):
+                raise OSError(errno.ENOBUFS, "injected tuning failure")
+            return super().setsockopt(*args)
+
+        def settimeout(self, timeout):
+            if failure == "framing" and timeout is None:
+                raise MemoryError("injected framing allocation failure")
+            return super().settimeout(timeout)
+
+        def close(self):
+            super().close()
+            if close_fails:
+                raise OSError(errno.EIO, "injected cleanup failure")
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(socket, "socket", FailingSocket)
+    endpoint = (
+        f"unix://{tmp_path / 'absent.sock'}"
+        if failure in ("connect", "timeout")
+        else listener.endpoint
+    )
+    try:
+        for _ in range(2):
+            with pytest.raises((TransportError, MemoryError)) as caught:
+                connect(endpoint, timeout=1)
+            errors.append(caught.value)
+        assert len(errors) == len(sockets) == 2
+        assert all(sock.fileno() == -1 for sock in sockets)
+        if close_fails:
+            assert all(
+                any("injected cleanup failure" in note for note in error.__notes__)
+                for error in errors
+            )
+    finally:
+        for sock in sockets:
+            socket.SocketType.close(sock)
+        listener.close()

+def test_send_frames_share_absolute_deadline(monkeypatch):
+    now = [10.0]
+    monkeypatch.setattr(transport, "time", Mock(monotonic=lambda: now[0]))
+    sock, peer_sock = socket.socketpair()
+    sock.settimeout(1)
+    peer = FramedConnection(peer_sock)
+
+    class MeteredSocket:
+        """Charge virtual time per byte, independent of send coalescing."""
+
+        def settimeout(self, timeout):
+            self.remaining = timeout
+
+        def sendall(self, data):
+            available = len(data) if self.remaining is None else self.remaining
+            sent = min(len(data), int(available))
+            if sent:
+                sock.sendall(data[:sent])
+            now[0] += min(len(data), available)
+            if sent != len(data):
+                raise TimeoutError
+
+        def shutdown(self, how):
+            sock.shutdown(how)
+
+        def close(self):
+            sock.close()
+
+    connection = FramedConnection(MeteredSocket())
+    try:

+        with pytest.raises(TransportTimeout):

+class ControlledExecutor(KVDigestExecutor):
+    def __init__(self, pool):
+        super().__init__(pool)
+        self.error = None
+        self.attempts = 0
+        self.failure_after = 0
+        self.gate = None
+        self.entered = threading.Event()
+
+    def execute(self, plan, features, *, num_speculative_tokens=None):
+        self.attempts += 1
+        if self.gate is not None:
+            self.entered.set()
+            assert self.gate.wait(5), "external executor was not released"
+        if self.error is not None and self.attempts >= self.failure_after:
+            raise self.error
+        return super().execute(
+            plan, features, num_speculative_tokens=num_speculative_tokens
+        )
+

+class ControlledAdapter(TargetConditionedDraftAdapter):
+    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
+        self.closed = threading.Event()
+        self.close_error = None
+
+    def close_sequences(self, keys):
+        if self.close_error is not None:
+            raise self.close_error
+        super().close_sequences(keys)
+        self.closed.set()

+def inputs(ids, tokens, positions, prefill, slots=None):
+    count = len(ids)
+    slots = slots if slots is not None else list(range(count))
+    lens = np.array([len(row) for row in tokens], dtype=np.int32)
+    indices = torch.tensor(slots, dtype=torch.int64)
+    starts = np.cumsum([0, *lens], dtype=np.int32)
+    computed = np.array([row[0] if row else 0 for row in positions], dtype=np.int32)
+    seq_lens = torch.from_numpy(computed + lens)
+    is_prefilling = np.array([length > 0 for length in prefill])
+    return InputBatch(
+        req_ids=ids,
+        num_reqs=count,
+        num_reqs_after_padding=count,
+        idx_mapping=indices,
+        idx_mapping_np=np.array(slots),
+        expanded_idx_mapping=indices,
+        expanded_local_pos=torch.zeros(count, dtype=torch.int32),
+        num_scheduled_tokens=lens,
+        num_tokens=int(sum(lens)),
+        num_tokens_after_padding=int(sum(lens)),
+        num_draft_tokens=0,
+        num_draft_tokens_per_req=None,
+        query_start_loc=torch.from_numpy(starts),
+        query_start_loc_np=starts,
+        seq_lens=seq_lens,
+        seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound=seq_lens,
+        dcp_local_seq_lens=None,
+        num_computed_tokens_np=computed,
+        prefill_len_np=np.array(prefill),
+        num_computed_prefill_tokens_np=computed,
+        is_prefilling_np=is_prefilling,
+        has_prefill=bool(is_prefilling.any()),
+        decode_graph_eligible=not is_prefilling.any(),
+        input_ids=torch.tensor(sum(tokens, []), dtype=torch.int32),
+        positions=torch.tensor(sum(positions, []), dtype=torch.int64),
+        is_padding=torch.zeros(int(sum(lens)), dtype=torch.bool),
+        logits_indices=torch.arange(count),
+        cu_num_logits=torch.arange(count + 1),
+        cu_num_logits_np=np.arange(count + 1),
+        has_structured_output_reqs=False,
+        prompt_lens=None,
+    )

+def propose(verifier, batch, sampled, rejected, recovery, lookahead=None, **kwargs):
+    last_sampled = torch.zeros(4, 1, dtype=torch.int64)
+    last_sampled[batch.idx_mapping, 0] = torch.tensor(recovery)
+    next_prefill = torch.zeros(1, 4, dtype=torch.int32)
+    if lookahead is not None:
+        next_prefill[0, batch.idx_mapping] = torch.tensor(lookahead, dtype=torch.int32)
+    return verifier.propose(
+        batch,
+        {},
+        {},
+        torch.zeros(batch.num_tokens, 16),
+        kwargs.pop("aux_hidden_states", None),
+        torch.tensor(sampled),
+        torch.tensor(rejected),
+        last_sampled,
+        next_prefill,
+        kwargs.pop("temperature", torch.zeros(4)),
+        torch.zeros(4, dtype=torch.int64),
+        **kwargs,
+    )

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Split-phase speculator proposal results.
+
+Splitting proposal generation into dispatch and collect lets a remote
+(dedicated-GPU) speculator overlap draft compute with target-side
+bookkeeping: dispatch returns a ProposalHandle that collect redeems for a
+SpeculatorOutput.
+"""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import torch
+
+
+@dataclass
+class SpeculatorOutput:
+    """Result of one proposal round.
+
+    ``valid_lengths`` decouples failure from token values: row ``i``
+    contributes ``token_ids[i, :valid_lengths[i]]`` draft tokens, and
+    ``valid_lengths[i] == 0`` means the request continues with target-only
+    decoding this round. Failures are never encoded as sentinel token IDs.
+    """
+
+    token_ids: torch.Tensor
+    """[batch, num_speculative_tokens] proposed draft token IDs."""
+    valid_lengths: torch.Tensor
+    """[batch] number of usable draft tokens per request."""
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        # Structural checks only; value-level checks would force a device
+        # sync on the hot path.
+        if self.token_ids.ndim != 2:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"token_ids must be 2-D [batch, K], got {self.token_ids.ndim}-D"
+            )
+        if self.valid_lengths.ndim != 1:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"valid_lengths must be 1-D [batch], got {self.valid_lengths.ndim}-D"
+            )
+        if self.token_ids.shape[0] != self.valid_lengths.shape[0]:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"batch size mismatch: token_ids has {self.token_ids.shape[0]} "
+                f"rows, valid_lengths has {self.valid_lengths.shape[0]}"
+            )
+        for name, tensor in (
+            ("token_ids", self.token_ids),
+            ("valid_lengths", self.valid_lengths),
+        ):
+            if tensor.is_floating_point() or tensor.is_complex():
+                raise ValueError(f"{name} must have an integer dtype")
+        if self.token_ids.device != self.valid_lengths.device:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"token_ids ({self.token_ids.device}) and valid_lengths "
+                f"({self.valid_lengths.device}) must be on the same device"
+            )
+
+
+class ProposalHandle:
+    """Opaque handle returned by dispatch, redeemed by collect."""

+"""Dedicated-device placement for target-conditioned own-KV speculators.
+
+This package contains the placement-independent building blocks for running
+EAGLE / P-EAGLE / native-MTP style speculators in a standalone process on a
+dedicated same-host GPU outside the target tensor-parallel group:
+
+- capabilities: what a speculator adapter/checkpoint supports and which
+  target features it needs every round.
+- protocol: control-plane message types exchanged between the verifier and
+  the standalone speculator server.
+- state: client-side handle/sequence state machines and the
+  placement-neutral batch/result types the session exposes to the runner.
+- transport: the framed inline stream transport (debug data plane).
+- session: the verifier-side session (handshake, sequence lifecycle,
+  dispatch/collect, failure latching).
+- server: the standalone server loop, idempotent sequence registry, the
+  adapter contract, and a deterministic fake adapter for tests.
+
+Only ``session`` operates on tensors. The server, protocol, registry, and
+state logic exchange raw data-plane frames, so they need no GPU and can be
+unit tested in isolation.
+"""
